title: Sam Dutrey's uncle and the Sister Kate trombone figure
summary: Joseph recalls meeting Sam at about 19 and a B-flat seventh figure on Sister Kate attributed to Sam's uncle, which he plays on the record with Paul.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Is there anything else you can tell us about Sam Duque? We'll finally catch up with him. I guess in an interview. You say you've been working that long, 23 years.
That's how long? Well, I can tell you, I see off and on. Let's say I was about, okay, I'm 41 now. I was about 19, about 19, 18, about 19 years old when I met Sam. I'm glad we're back.
I think a few more things I think we can talk about to fill up some of this. We don't have to fill it all up necessarily. Did you ever know Sam's father? No, no. Old man Sam.
No, I heard of his uncle. Matter of fact, it's a little deal I use now on Sister Kate when I was told his uncle uses it.
On Norrie. Yeah. I liked it, you know. What was that, what part was that? I don't remember. I mean, ever hearing about that. I don't think he ever recorded the…
Well, I don't know if he recorded, but I heard that he used to use it, you know. It's just a B flat, seven chord he run, you know.
I know there's some part in there, they sort of hold some long notes, slide up, can you, can you, can you hum it or sing it in any way?
I know it's hard to demonstrate without the trombone, but it's…
Dun, No, I don't really, it, I made it on this, uh, deal with Paul.
Well, it's on the one with Paul. Yeah, yeah. But we'll, if we don't have that, we'll get a copy sooner or later. That record is cut out, but I think I saved one for Tulane on there.
Yeah, yeah, I like that. It's really…
So it was on that Sister Kate, I forget what the Zone went right.

But I don't know if Sam's uncle made it on the record, but Paul told me, you know, as a matter of fact, too. But you know, you like to hear a cat play a thing a long time, you know, and you hear someone else play, you say, well man, so and so done it, you know. Yeah. But it just happened, you keep running the B flat 7 chord, you know, the way you run it.

Yeah, we'll have to get that, because Dutry did record with King Oliver, and that's about the only band he recorded with up north, Joe Oliver and that group. They never made Sister Kate, I'm sure, because I haven't just about every Oliver record made. Did you ever get to hear Dutry in person? Oh, no, no, no. He left almost before you were born, I guess, and went north about that time.
No, I never did hear him, no. I saw some pictures of him. I can see the resemblance of Sam, though.
